hypotheses.hypothesis: GenAI is now material revenue, not a pilot-stage side line.
hypotheses.test: AI share of revenue at disclosing firms; size of the eight-firm AI pool.
hypotheses.evidence: TCS 10.1% and Infosys 10.5% of revenue (company-disclosed); eight-firm AI run-rate ~$15.8 bn (range $13.2-18.9 bn), ~7.6% of their combined revenue. TCS's AI run-rate rose 72% in three quarters ($1.8 bn to $3.1 bn).
hypotheses.so_what: AI is now big enough to move the P&L. The open question has shifted from 'is AI real?' to 'is AI net-additive?'.

hypotheses.hypothesis: AI revenue growth is arriving alongside a shrinking core business (AI deflation).
hypotheses.test: Split revenue into AI and non-AI at two points for every firm with an AI time series; annualise each.
hypotheses.evidence: Core (non-AI) revenue shrank at all three Indian disclosers: Infosys -5.9%/yr, TCS -3.6%/yr, HCLTech -0.5%/yr, while total revenue grew only 2.2-2.4%. Accenture's core still grew +4.7% (FY24-FY25).
hypotheses.verdict: Directionally supported for TCS and Infosys (upper bound; TCS core rests on two data points); weaker for HCLTech; not for Accenture
hypotheses.so_what: At TCS and Infosys, AI growth is so far replacing core revenue, not adding to it. That fits the 2-3.5%/yr deflation analysts cite. Part of the shift may be existing work relabelled as AI, which no firm discloses.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The firms with the most AI revenue are not the ones growing fastest.
hypotheses.test: Spearman rank correlation between AI share of revenue and constant-currency revenue growth (8 firms; and the 4 company-based disclosers).
hypotheses.evidence: Rank correlation -0.05 across all eight (p=0.91) and -0.40 across the four disclosers (n=4, not testable). Five of the eight AI shares are estimates or peer benchmarks. Infosys (10.5% AI) grew 1.5%; TCS (10.1%) 2.8%; Capgemini (est. 8%) 11.7% incl. WNS; Tech Mahindra (est. 5%) 7.2%.
hypotheses.verdict: Weak: no positive link in this sample (n=8, not significant)
hypotheses.so_what: 'AI revenue' is not yet a growth KPI. For CI and investor work, track core growth and book-to-bill next to the AI number.

hypotheses.hypothesis: AI has decoupled revenue from headcount.
hypotheses.test: Revenue growth minus headcount growth (YoY), and revenue per employee.
hypotheses.evidence: Median gap only +1.4pp. Six of eight show weak or no decoupling. Revenue per employee rose 0.5-1.7% at most firms; Tech Mahindra is the outlier (+6.9%, headcount down). Capgemini's headcount jumped 18% with the WNS acquisition.
hypotheses.so_what: Productivity gains are being passed to clients as price, not kept as margin or non-linear growth. That is the deflation mechanism in H2 seen from the people side.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Announcement momentum (Project 1's CI events) predicts AI monetisation.
hypotheses.test: Spearman rank correlation of verified Project 1 events per firm against AI share of revenue and against growth.
hypotheses.evidence: Rank correlations (n=8): events vs AI share -0.14 (p=0.75); events vs growth -0.57 (p=0.14, not significant). HCLTech and Cognizant lead on event count (12 each), with TCS and Wipro on 11. Wipro's revenue is flat and it discloses no AI revenue; Capgemini has no frontier-lab ties and the fastest growth (11.7% incl. WNS).
hypotheses.verdict: No evidence of a link (n=8, not significant)
hypotheses.so_what: Partnership press releases are a weak lead indicator. A CI programme should weight disclosed AI revenue, core growth and bookings above announcement counts - the main design lesson carried back to Project 1.

Bear.story: Renewal repricing passes the full ~3.5%/yr AI deflation to clients (Kotak base case) with no volume offset; AI growth fades fast as pilots stall.

Base.story: Core drifts from today's ~+1% organic to -1.5%/yr as large contracts renew at AI-adjusted prices; AI growth halves from today's ~70-80% and keeps decelerating.

Bull.story: Clients reinvest about half of AI savings in new work (Kotak's offset), so core stays slightly positive; agentic AI programmes scale quickly.
